title: Authorization chaos testing and evidence capture protocol
content:
Purpose:
This document defines a repeatable, low-risk protocol for running controlled chaos experiments against RBAC v2 and related entitlement plumbing to validate:
  - audit/evidence capture fidelity (fields, timestamps, correlation ids)
  - SIEM export transformations and size/throughput characteristics
  - safe rollback/mitigation behavior when entitlements are corrupted or delayed

Why chaos for authorization?
Authorization is a cross-cutting system: policy engines, attribute services, feature flags, and tokens all interact. Subtle timing or partial failures can produce either silent permission leaks or opaque denials. Traditional unit/integration tests miss forensics and telemetry gaps — chaos experiments exercise real observability and evidence pipelines under degraded conditions.

Scope and constraints
  - Scope: RBAC v2 control plane (policy store, resolution service), entitlement caching, audit-event producer, and SIEM export adapter.
  - Allowed targets: canary namespaces and a dedicated test org in staging only. Never run against prod tenants.
  - Safety controls: automatic throttles, kill-switch webhook, and pre-registered blast radius keys. All experiments require a run owner and SRE observer.

Experiment categories
  1) Mutation tests — change entitlement graph nodes (roles -> permissions) mid-flight to validate evidence and rollback.
  2) Timing tests — inject delays in attribute services and token introspection to force cache staleness.
  3) Loss tests — drop audit events at producer (simulate network loss) and validate replay/seq numbers and SIEM reconciliation.
  4) Schema evolution tests — rotate audit schema (add optional fields, rename keys) and exercise SIEM transformation layer.

Test matrix (example)
  - Scenario A: Role rename propagation delay (mutation + timing)
      * Target: staging-org-chi, test-users 50
      * Actions: rename role 'data-analyst' -> 'data-insights' while producing queries that depend on role name in entitlements cache.
      * Expected: all authorization decisions remain consistent or are safely denied; audit log shows prior role and new role with correlation id; SIEM has both records linked.
  - Scenario B: Audit producer network partition (loss)
      * Target: staging-export-adapter
      * Actions: drop 10% of outbound audit events for 15 minutes; trigger replay and reconciliation job.
      * Expected: sequence gaps detectability, replay executes, SIEM reconciliation marks recovered vs unrecoverable events.

Evidence capture requirements
Every authorization event emitted during chaos must include the following minimal fields (these are required for postmortem and SIEM correlation):
  - event_id (UUID)
  - event_type (authorization_decision / entitlement_change / cache_eviction / replay_status)
  - actor_id (user/service principal id)
  - resource (string identifier e.g., /orgs/abc/datasets/123)
  - permission (canonical permission name)
  - decision (allow|deny|deferred)
  - reason_code (optional short code for automation)
  - policy_version (semantic version or unique id)
  - correlation_id (propagated across calls)
  - timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
  - evidence_blob_ref (pointer to snapshot of relevant inputs: attributes, token claims, cached-keys)

Sample audit event (stringified JSON for clarity):
  '{"event_id":"9f3a2d6e-1c4a-4b5f-9a3e-11c7b0f0a1d2","event_type":"authorization_decision","actor_id":"svc-ingest-9","resource":"/project/x/dataset/metrics","permission":"dataset.read","decision":"deny","reason_code":"ATTR_TIMEOUT","policy_version":"v2.3.1","correlation_id":"corr-20250122-72","timestamp_utc":"2025-01-22T14:12:07Z","evidence_blob_ref":"s3://evidence/staging/corr-20250122-72/snapshot-1.json"}'

SIEM export expectations and transformations
  - Exporter must preserve event_id and correlation_id. SIEM should receive a flattened record with key fields indexed for search.
  - For high-volume simulations we expect peak throughput tests: 5k auth events/sec for 30s bursts. Export path must batch and drop downsample tags rather than losing correlation ids.
  - Transformation rules: map policy_version -> policy_id, evidence_blob_ref -> evidence_link, convert timestamp_utc to epoch_ms field siem_ts.

Replay and reconciliation protocol
  - Each producer maintains a monotonic sequence per partition and writes sequence checkpoints to durable store.
  - When loss is detected (gap in seq) the producer should attempt replay and emit replay_status events: {status: started|completed|failed, recovered_count, unrecoverable_count}.
  - SIEM must annotate original gap and replay events, and the postmortem should include recovered/unrecoverable counts.

Automation and tooling
  - authz-sim-harness: a lightweight simulator that can drive mutations, inject timing faults, and capture evidence snapshots. Located at github.com/redwood-inference/authz-sim-harness (linked above).
  - evidence-collector: cron job that, during an experiment, snapshots attribute service responses and token claims and uploads them to a dedicated evidence bucket. Snapshot keys match the correlation_id naming scheme.

Runbook (step-by-step)
  1) Planning: define hypothesis, blast radius, target test org, and rollback criteria. Document in the experiment ticket.
  2) Preflight: verify canary org exists, smoke tests pass, and data retention policy for evidence is set (14 days by default).
  3) Register run with SRE and security observer. Register kill-switch URL and escalate contacts.
  4) Execute in stages: baseline collection (5m), perturbation (configurable), steady-state (10m), recovery (run replay/reconciliation), and verification (validate SIEM records and evidence blobs).
  5) Postmortem: collect all correlation_ids, evidence blobs, SIEM exported snapshots, and produce a play-by-play timeline. Fill out the postmortem template and link to the experiment ticket.

Success criteria
  - 100% of emitted events during perturbation include event_id and correlation_id.
  - Replay recovers > 95% of dropped events in loss simulations.
  - SIEM transformation preserves traceability (can link an SIEM row back to an evidence_blob_ref).

Failure modes and mitigation
  - Unbounded replay backlog: pause new experiments, triage consumer lag, and increase replay concurrency or reduce blast radius.
  - Evidence blob missing: mark event as partially unverifiable; capture affected correlation_ids for retention extension and deeper forensic capture.
  - Schema incompatibility: fallback exporter to prior schema version and flag transformation errors to the export-alerting channel.

Artifacts to produce after each run
  - run-summary.md (timeline, hypothesis, outcome)
  - evidence-index.csv (one row per correlation_id with evidence_blob_ref and checksum)
  - siem-export-sample.json (first 1000 flattened records)
  - postmortem link and action items (owner + due date)

Open questions and next work
  - Should evidence_blob_refs be signed (HMAC) to guarantee immutability? Pros/cons and storage costs to be evaluated.
  - Retention: default 14 days may be insufficient for long-tail investigations — proposal to add tiered retention for high-risk tenants.
  - Canary expansion: how to safely move experiments into limited production with customer opt-in.

Appendix: quick-check checklist for experiment owners
  - [ ] Confirm staging org and canaries are healthy
  - [ ] Register run ticket and SRE on-call
  - [ ] Verify evidence bucket retention and access controls
  - [ ] Smoke test SIEM export pipeline with a synthetic event
  - [ ] Ensure kill-switch and alerting channels are configured

Notes: This is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive: the goal is to find gaps in observability and evidence pipelines before they show up in customer incidents. Keep experiments small, documented, and reversible.
